content:
For years there has been this issue in mathlib that we have a concrete definition of elliptic curve over a ring (which is necessary for some concrete calculations) rather than the abstract definition. The concrete definition works fine for fields and there are many applications of the theory over fields (for example the LMFDB uses our definition of elliptic curve).

For the definition of elliptic curve over a scheme (which we don't have) we will be faced with the same question: abstract or concrete. The abstract definition is something like "smooth rel dim 1 proper group scheme with geom connected fibres", the concrete one is "scheme over S with a section which locally at each point looks like an elliptic Weierstrass model where the section is the section at infinity". Several groups want modular curves and I simply cannot see a path to a meaningful definition of modular curve in the algebraic category without a definition of elliptic curve over a scheme; furthermore rather than having to make the choice between the abstract and concrete definition I am wondering whether we can now be more ambitious and think about proving that these definitions are the same.

The fact that the abstract and concrete definitions of elliptic curve coincide will need some form of Riemann-Roch and my understanding is that this is currently an ongoing student project so my instinct is to stay away. But thinking about it, I realise that there is actually plenty more stuff we need as well as RR. Here is a sketch of just the beginning of the argument relating abstract and concrete elliptic curves, stopping before RR kicks in. How far are we from (a) the definitions and (b) the proofs of these results? There is a lot of stuff here; I have not really thought about this question before because I was waiting for RR and I only really just internalised the fact that as well as RR there is a ton of other stuff which one needs.

Step 1: let E/S be an elliptic curve over a scheme in the abstract sense (smooth proper group scheme etc). Then E is smooth so locally of finite presentation, and proper hence quasi-compact hence of finite presentation.

Q1) Hopefully everything is easy so far?

Step 2: Hence we can cover S by open affines U_i such that on each U_i, E is the pullback to U_i of an abstract elliptic curve over Spec(R_i), with R_i a Noetherian ring (this is the standard "reduction to the Noetherian case" of EGA IV sections 8ff).

Q2) This might be harder than you think, because it's not just descending E as a scheme, it's descending E as a smooth proper group scheme. Are we a long way from this? There is a basic theory of reduction to the Noetherian case (if f:X->Y is of finite presentation then there's f_0:X_0 -> Y_0 a finitely presented map of Noetherian schemes and Y -> Y_0 such that X is the pullback of X_0, which would already be a cool result to have; the hard part is results of the form "if f has property P then f_0 can also be taken to have property P and IIRC if P="flat" then this is rather more subtle than you might think, although I don't remember how hard "smooth", "proper" and "has group scheme structure" are to descend).

Step 3) We now need a key finiteness result. If f:E->S is a proper morphism between Noetherian schemes and F is a coherent sheaf on E then the derived pushforwards Rif∗(F)R^if_*(F)Rif∗​(F) are all coherent on SSS. This is a fancy relative generalisation of the statement "coherent sheaf cohomology of a projective/proper variety is finite-dimensional".

Q3) Can we even state this? I know there has been a lot of work recently on derived functors and on quasicoherent sheaves of modules; perhaps this is a great test case. I am not suggesting that we're close to proving it. The proof is EGA III, 3.2.1 .

Step 4) If n is a positive integer and e:S->E is the identity section of the group scheme (and recall E->S is smooth rel dim 1) then we need the coherent sheaf O(ne)\mathcal{O}(ne)O(ne) on E associated to the Cartier divisor nenene.

Q4) Are we in a position to write down this standard construction of invertible sheaves on a Noetherian scheme associated to Cartier divisors?

Step 5) If Y is affine, f:X->Y is proper, if F is a coherent sheaf on X, flat over Y, and if for some natural n we have H^{n+1}(X_p,F_p)=0 for all points p of Y, then R^nf_*F commutes with all base changes.

Q5) Again can we state this? The proof is in Mumford abelian varieties (p53 of my hard copy).

The next step uses RR for fields (the fibres X_p in the application are now smooth proper curves over fields) so I'll stop there, but it hadn't really dawned on me what a vast amount of stuff one actually needed before RR (unless anyone knows a better way of getting to the statement that every elliptic curve over a scheme is locally a Weierstrass equation; the argument I've presented here is the one in Katz-Mazur).

About Q3, it would not be too hard to formalize the statement. The main remaining thing is the existence of the derived functors, and for that we basically need to know that categories of sheaves of modules have enough injectives. A similar proof as for sheaves of abelian groups should be possible.

module

public import Mathlib.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Sheaf.Quasicoherent
public import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Modules.Sheaf
public import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.Proper
public import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Noetherian
public import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Abelian.GrothendieckCategory.EnoughInjectives
public import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Abelian.RightDerived

universe u

open CategoryTheory

namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme

example {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [IsProper f] [IsLocallyNoetherian Y]
    (M : X.Modules) [M.IsFinitePresentation] (n : ℕ) :
    (((Modules.pushforward f).rightDerived n).obj M).IsFinitePresentation := sorry

end AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme
Wow thanks! There's a pretty cool challenge then :-)

CategoryTheory.Functor.rightDerived is currently defined using rightDerivedToHomotopyCategory together with HomotopyCategory.homologyFunctor. There is a TODO item suggesting it will be refactored by combining DerivedCategory.Plus.singleFunctor, CategoryTheory.Functor.rightDerivedFunctorPlus, and DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor.

If we don't just want to write down statements but also work towards (auto-)proving them, do you recommend that we use the old rightDerived, or write down the intended new definition and work with it instead?

The old (current) definition is a dead end. The new definition is https://github.com/joelriou/mathlib4/blob/jriou_localization/Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/DerivedCategory/RightDerivedFunctorPlus.lean#L236
